newsitem.title: GERMANY: Size of income tax cut not yet decided -- Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Size of income tax cut not yet decided -- Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in an interview to be published on Monday that it had not been decided whether a controversial surcharge on income tax would be cut by one or two points in 1998.

The "solidarity surcharge," intended to pay for German reunification, has prompted a row between Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) and the liberal Free Democrats (FDP), both junior partners in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition.
Earlier this month a growing budget deficit forced the FDP, the self-styled party of tax cuts, to agree to postpone a cut in the 7.5 percent surcharge to Jan. 1998 from July 1997.
The FDP says the agreement means that the full two-point cut will still be implemented with a six-month delay.
However, top CSU officials say the cut could be less, and CSU general secretary Bernd Protzner told Sunday's weekly Welt am Sonntag it was not certain there would be any cut at all.
Waigel told the Augsburger Allgemeine daily, according to an advance release, that the tax would be cut in 1998.
He said there would be a decision "at the appropriate time" about whether this cut would be one point or two.
"That's what it says in our agreement and that's the way it will be," he said.
